title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order and unable to be put in order because Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and therefore lacked standing (line 19). The decision was approved 23-0 on a roll call, with one absent (line 21).
first_summary: The SJC held Benyola's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery administratively out of order because he was no longer a PCA member and lacked standing; the vote was 23-0, one absent. The underlying complaint and any merits are not described.
summary: The SJC declared Benyola's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order, because Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and thus lacked standing. The decision was adopted 23-0 on a roll call, one absent, on the officers' recommendation. The record does not identify the underlying presbytery action or reach the complaint's merits, so the case's value is its threshold standing ruling, not any complaint determination.
